creator: Alexander Terp
description:
amterp, Chat Notes 2026-10-14: "mechanism for messaging between agents which doesn't just enter thru pane, since that can be blocked or occupied. what about something involving monitors maybe?"

The doorbell types a wake into an agent's pane, and that fails when the prompt holds a draft, a dialog covers it, or it is not on screen: a_2izzXOqQF, a_2hIfuUkdQ, a_2hL5I8kn2 and a_2hIfvZQJP are all this.

A way around the doorbell exists for Claude Code and Codex. `extras/claude-code/messaging-hooks.json` and `extras/codex/messaging-hooks.json` hand an agent its messages after each tool call, and Claude Code's background `Stop` hook starts a turn when a wake is due (`muster docs msg`). But it is opt-in per session, through `--settings`, and kept out of the plugin so that not every session with the plugin takes part in messaging. So an agent started in a pane the usual way is rung.

Questions:

- Should an agent Muster starts in a pane get the messaging hooks by default? Or should the hooks ship in the plugin and do nothing until the pane joins a group?
- Claude Code's `Stop` hook misses a session that went idle after Esc or an API error. Would its Monitor tool, watching `muster msg wait`, cover that?
- Which agents would still need the doorbell: harnesses with no hooks, and sessions that opted out.
title: Should agents in panes get their messages without anything typed into their prompt?
